newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore spends S$5 bln on legal gambling in 1996.
newsitem.headline: Singapore spends S$5 bln on legal gambling in 1996.

text.p: Singaporeans placed some S$5 billion (US$3.5 billion) on legal bets in 1996 and an estimated S$20 billion could have gone to illegal gambling, the Straits Times newspaper reported on Sunday.
A cut in betting duty in 1995 had encouraged more gamblers to go for legalised betting, promoting a 19 percent jump in the business in 1996, the report said.
However, illegal gambling conducted in casinos or on cruise ships continued, with industry officials estimating the turnover at S$20 billion (US$14 billion), it said.

The money that went to legal horse-racing, jackpot machines and Singapore's Sweep and Toto lottery games was still far behind that in Hong Kong, where S$14.7 billion (US$10.3 billion) was spent on horse-racing alone in 1996, the newspaper said.
